english.title: Occupier fail to provide means of cleansing and disinfection to infected premises
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the occupier upon whom a notice under regulation 7 of the Diseases of Swine Regulations 2014 had been served designating premises at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) as suspect premises, failed to

(A)_[provide and maintain means of cleansing and disinfection at the entrances to, and exits from, the premises and all buildings on those premises housing pigs,]_
(B)_[comply with directions from an inspector concerning such means of cleansing and disinfection and the imposition of other biosecurity measures including rodent and vector control,]_

in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 6 of Schedule 1 to and regulation 39(1)(p) and (2) of the Diseases of Swine Regulations 2014.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time Limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
